Arsonist Starts Fire At Golders Green Apartment Building
content:
An arsonist started a fire in a stairwell of a Golders Green apartment building where most of the residents are Jewish, and many are young families, the Shomrim organization in London reported.
The incident began when a fire alarm went off in the early hours of Tuesday morning. Residents reported that they witnessed a suspect deliberately setting a fire in the stairwell. He fled the scene when confronted by residents.
One of the residents acted quickly to extinguish the fire, preventing what could have turned into a far more serious incident. B’Chasdei Hashem, no injuries were reported.
Shomrim volunteers collected evidence believed to belong to the arsonist and transferred it to the police.
The disturbing incident comes less than a month after two Jews were seriously injured in a stabbing incident in Golders Green and two months after four Hatzolah ambulances were set on fire in Golders Green.
(YWN Israel Desk—Jerusalem)

title: Explosion and fire at a Dallas apartment building kills at least 3 people , including a child
content:
Explosion and fire at a Dallas apartment building kills at least 3 people, including a child
DALLAS (AP) — An explosion and massive fire at a Dallas apartment building Thursday killed a child and at least two other people following a blast that shook nearby homes and happened while firefighters were rushing to a reported gas leak, officials said.
At least five people also went to hospitals with injuries, Dallas Fire-Rescue spokesperson Jason Evans said. It was unclear how many residents lived in the two-story complex in the Oak Cliff neighborhood south of downtown Dallas, where a towering plume of black smoke was visible for miles.
Evans did not rule out that more victims could be found as crews continued to sift through the charred remains of the building. By late Thursday, Evans said firefighters had searched less than half of the scene by hand and that some areas would require excavation.
“This was enormous,” Evans said of the fire.
As dozens of firefighters swarmed to the neighborhood, some residents’ friends and relatives worried as they tried unsuccessfully to reach each loved ones. Dozens of firefighters searched through the smoldering rubble of the building even as colleagues continued to drench the blackened debris.
Berry said firefighters were responding to a call of a gas leak when an explosion happened.
“We had the cavalry coming,” Dallas Fire-Rescue Deputy Chief Mark Berry said. ”But the explosion had already taken place.”
Atmos Energy, a natural gas provider, said in a statement they were told by fire officials that a construction crew unrelated to the company had damaged a pipeline near the site of the fire.
Kacee Proctor, a resident of the apartment building, said her mother had smelled gas inside a day earlier, but Proctor didn’t think much of it at the time.
She wasn’t home during the blast and was devastated that her cat, Shirley, was stuck inside.
“I’ve been sitting over there crying for several hours. I don’t know what to do. This is all I have right here,” Proctor said, gesturing to the clothes she was wearing.
She spent the afternoon chatting with neighbors who had evacuated, including a girl who was home babysitting her little sister and carried both the child and their dog to safety.
Natural gas service to the area remained shut off, and company officials were working with investigators on-site, the company said.
Authorities set up a family reunification center at a nearby high school. Several hours after the blaze, Frances Rizo was still trying to find her friend who lived in the building.
“She’s not answering her phone,” Rizo said.
Firefighters rushed to the scene as flames and black smoke billowed into the sky. Some trained their hoses on piles of smoking debris while others removed lumber and other burned wreckage to look for anyone trapped underneath. Little more than a blackened shell of the original building remained.
“The fire is contained, but our members are still working on the scene to do primary searches,” said Dallas Fire-Rescue Assistant Chief James Russ.
Julie Jensen said she was at home less than a block from the burning building when she heard a noise like an explosion that left her ears ringing.
“I was sitting on my couch watching TV — stuff flew off our walls,” Jensen said.
Jensen said she saw rising smoke and neighbors running when she looked out the window. She grabbed her family’s cat and left, finding a nearby parking lot to wait until she knew it was safe to return.
Sal De La Rosa was at work at a nearby auto repair shop when “all of a sudden we just heard and felt this huge boom.”
“We felt where the building kind of shook a little bit,” De La Rosa said.
He said a co-worker went outside and saw thick, black smoke rising into the air.
___
This story has been updated to correct the spelling of Frances Rizo’s last name in one instance. It is Rizo, not Rizzo.
___
Associated Press journalists Jim Vertuno in Austin, Texas, Russ Bynum in Savannah, Georgia, and Hannah Schoenbaum in Salt Lake City contributed.

Skokie apartment fire: Elderly woman seriously injured, witness describes chaos
SKOKIE, Ill. - A late-night fire at a Skokie apartment building sent an 84-year-old woman to the hospital and reportedly left residents scrambling to get out.
What we know:
Firefighters and police responded around 10:08 p.m. Monday to a multifamily building in the 9500 block of Bronx Place and found heavy smoke on the third floor, according to the Skokie Fire Department.
Crews contained the fire to a single unit within about 20 minutes.
Officials said one resident, an 84-year-old woman, was seriously injured and taken to an area hospital.
What they're saying:
A resident described the chaotic moment as neighbors rushed to warn one another.
"I started hearing like people running within the hallways of my building, people knocking, banging on doors, screaming," she said.
What we don't know:
The cause of the fire is still unknown, and no damage estimate was immediately available.
What's next:
The unit where the fire broke out was deemed uninhabitable, but all other residents were allowed back into their homes once crews completed their work.
The Source: The information in this story came from the Skokie Fire Department and a witness interview.

content:
More than 20 firefighters, supported by six vehicles—including a specialized aerial platform—responded to a major fire that broke out in an apartment on the first floor of a residential building in Drapetsona, a suburb of Piraeus in Attica. Elderly Resident Refuses Evacuation
An elderly woman residing on the third floor has refused to leave her home despite repeated efforts by firefighters and police officers. Emergency responders have administered oxygen due to smoke inhalation and continue working to safely evacuate her.

content:
South County firefighters rescue 2 people, dog from third-floor apartment fire
SNOHOMISH COUNTY, Wash. — Two adults and a dog were rescued from a third-floor apartment window after a fire tore through a Mountlake Terrace apartment building early Sunday, displacing more than a dozen households.
Firefighters responded to the Taluswood Apartments in the 4300 block of 236th St. SW shortly after 12 a.m. and found heavy smoke and fire coming from a three-story building. Crews spotted two adults at a window of an upper-floor unit and used a ladder to rescue both people and a dog.
The man and woman, both approximately in their 20s, were taken to Swedish Edmonds Hospital in stable condition and have since been discharged. The dog did not require medical intervention.
Fire spread across the second and third floors and into the attic of the impacted building. Firefighters searched 12 primarily affected units and evacuated residents from 12 adjacent units. Everyone else escaped safely, officials said.
After the fire was controlled, crews continued extinguishing hotspots until about 2 a.m. One firefighter was treated at the scene for a minor injury. Two additional civilians were evaluated by firefighters and did not require further medical care.
Residents in 13 apartment units were displaced, including at least 24 adults, one child, and 15 pets. Support 7 and American Red Cross volunteers are assisting those residents with immediate needs.
The Snohomish County Fire Marshal’s Office is investigating the cause of the fire. Damage estimates were not yet available. Shoreline Fire and Bothell Fire Department assisted in the response.
Fire officials also urged residents to have a home fire escape plan and working smoke alarms, noting that modern homes can burn faster due to synthetic furniture and open layouts. Smoke alarms should be replaced every 10 years and installed in every bedroom, outside every sleeping area, and on every level of a home.

Firefighters save dozens from midnight apartment fire in Mountlake Terrace, WA
EVERETT, Wash. - A late night fire north of Seattle caused a large response from area firefighters as they worked to rescue people and pets from the apartment building. In total, 24 adults, one child and 15 pets have been displaced by the fire.
Timeline:
Just after midnight heading into Sunday morning, South County firefighters were dispatched to a three-story apartment building in Mountlake Terrace on 236th Street SW.
Two people were reportedly spotted asking for help from a third floor window. Firefighters were able to get a ladder up to them and a dog to rescue them. Meanwhile, additional firefighters were called in to assist with the growing fire.
The 2-alarm fire caused residents from 12 apartments to be evacuated. Firefighting personnel spent more than two hours putting the fire out and addressing hot spots on the structure to prevent ignition.

Dog killed after fire fills Cincinnati apartment building with smoke
CINCINNATI (WKRC) - A dog died after a fire filled a west side Cincinnati apartment building with smoke Tuesday morning, according to fire officials.
Crews with Green Township Fire & EMS responded around 9:18 a.m. to the 6700 block of Harrison Avenue after receiving reports of smoke throughout the apartment complex.
Firefighters arrived to find a working fire inside a second-floor apartment and quickly launched an interior attack. Officials said the fire was brought under control by 9:33 a.m.
One dog died from smoke exposure, but no residents or firefighters were injured.
Multiple fire departments responded to assist, including crews from Miami Township, Cheviot, Whitewater Township and Colerain Township.
The cause of the apartment fire remains under investigation, though officials said it is not considered suspicious.

title: Residents displaced , one treated for smoke inhalation after apartment complex fire
content:
Residents displaced, one treated for smoke inhalation after apartment complex fire
SAN ANTONIO - A large fire at a two-story apartment building early Saturday morning has displaced multiple residents and caused extensive damage to the complex.
The fire started around 7:30 a.m., with fire crews arriving to find heavy flames spreading across both the first and second floors of the building. Due to the intensity of the fire, additional resources were requested, and crews were forced to shift to a defensive strategy, battling the fire from outside.
At least half of the building is expected to be a total loss. All residents of the affected building have been displaced as a result of the fire.
One person was evaluated and treated at the scene for minor smoke inhalation.
Apartment management is on-site working to help residents find temporary housing, and the Red Cross is on standby to provide additional assistance if needed.

title: Two rescued from Kansas apartment fire , 3 pets died
content:
RILEY COUNTY—Two people were rescued and hospitalized after an apartment fire in Manhattan.
At 6:13 a.m. on Tuesday, the Manhattan Fire Department was dispatched to an apartment building fire at 509 Pierre Street in Manhattan, according to a media release. Upon arrival, crews found a two-story residential building with smoke and flames showing from the second floor, and two persons on the porch roof.
A passerby had put up a ladder, climbed onto the porch roof, and helped an occupant out of a second-floor window and onto the porch roof.
The driver of firetruck Quint 2 raised a fire department ladder, allowing the two to come down. Firefighters then entered the building to search for another occupant reported to be trapped inside.
Firefighters found the person unconscious on the second floor and quickly removed them from the building. Both occupants of the second-floor apartment were transported by Riley County EMS.
There were four occupants of the building in total, with two escaping the first-floor apartment fire prior to the fire department's arrival. The passerby was uninjured. One dog was transported by Riley County Animal Control to Kansas State Vet Med. Two dogs and a cat perished in the fire.
The cause of the fire is under investigation at this time. The Kansas State Fire Marshal's Office and Riley County Police Department are assisting Manhattan Fire Investigators with the investigation.

content:
Chimney fire at Tower Point Condominiums prompts swift evacuation; no injuries reported
John Garcia arrived at the Tower Point Condominiums to see what was happening after smelling smoke from a friend’s house.
When he got there, he saw flames coming from a 12-unit apartment building in the middle of the complex.
“It was kinda chaos,” said Garcia.
RELATED: Residents urged to inspect chimneys after fire devastates Tower Point Condominiums
Garcia recorded video as he ran up to the burning apartment building. In the footage, flames can be seen on the roof. Fire officials say they believe the fire started in a chimney and then spread to the roof.
“The entire chimney itself was on fire,” said Joe Arrington with the San Antonio Fire Department.
When firefighters arrived, they immediately began evacuating people from the building. The apartment building was located in the center of the complex, just feet away from other buildings. One of those nearby residents was Kaitlyn Kennedy, whose apartment is right next door.
“The windows are gonna be really smoky, and there might be some warping to those too,” said Kennedy.
Eventually, the third floor of the building collapsed into the second floor. That’s when firefighters moved into a defensive position, spraying water from ladder trucks.
“There was a couple with their kids that just got out of the house,” said Garcia. “She was barefooted. I think the husband just got home.”
Fire officials say no one was hurt, and no other buildings caught fire.
“If the wind was going the other way, it probably would have been a lot different,” said neighbor Ellen Jensen.
Red Cross representatives say everyone who lost there home has a place to sleep. If you are affected by the fire and need help you can reach out to 800-733-2767.

content:
Fire breaks out in major London tower with black smoke seen
Several workers were forced to evacuate as a fire started in a major London tower, with a huge convoy of 60 firefighters flocking to the scene containing billowing black smoke
A huge fire has broken out in Canary Wharf, with black smoke seen billowing from a tower. A Morgan Stanley fire marshall told the Express the entire building has been evacuated.
Multiple fire engines can be seen parking outside, with part of the top floor of The Cabot in Canary Wharf currently on fire. The fire in on 25 Cabot Square, which is a 17-floor office building occupied by Morgan Stanley in Canary Wharf. One employee in the building told the Express: “It’s an electrical fire on the roof. We’ve all been told to leave”.
While it has not yet been confirmed what caused the fire, black smoke can be seen covering the skyline above the tower.
It is also understood that the road next to the building has been halted, with no traffic allowed to pass by the fire. The whole building has been evacuated, with workers lining up on the street, but it is not yet known how many floors have been affected.
A security officer has told the Express that it would be "a very long time" before workers would be allowed back into the building.
A statement from the London Fire Brigade says: "Eight fire engines and around 60 firefighters have been called to a fire in an electrical intake room on Cabot Square in Canary Wharf.
"An electrical intake room on the top floor of the building is currently alight.
"The Brigade was called at 1713 and is still on scene. The Brigade's 999 Control officers received 15 calls alerting them to the fire. They deployed crews from Poplar, Shadwell, Whitechapel, Plaistow, Dowgate, Euston, Dockhead, Shoreditch, Lewisham and East Greenwich fire stations.
"The cause of the fire is not known at this stage."
As well as the huge firefighter presence, an image from the scene shows numerous ambulances at the scene, with tape to cordon off an area next to the building in Canary Wharf.
Taking to X, London Fire Brigade wrote: "Eight fire engines and around 60 firefighters have been called to a fire in an electrical intake room on Cabot Square in #CanaryWharf. More info soon."
They later said the fire was due to an electrical issue. Writing on X, he said: "An electrical intake room on the top floor of a building in #CanaryWharf is currently alight. Our 999 Control officers have received 15 calls alerting them to the fire."

title: Portland apartment fire injures 3 , including firefighter in rescue
Firefighter injured , resident hospitalized in Portland apartment fire rescue
content:
Firefighter injured, resident hospitalized in Portland apartment fire rescue
PORTLAND, Ore. (KATU) — Portland Fire & Rescue crews faced a challenging Sunday morning as they responded to two separate fire incidents in the Northwest District.
The first call came just before 9 a.m. for a fire at a two-story apartment building located at 1233 NW 23rd and Overton.
Crews reported heavy fire and smoke from a second-story window once they arrived, with a person trapped inside.
Firefighters handled the blaze, while a separate fire truck conducted a vent/enter/isolate/search operation to rescue the trapped resident.
The person was then safely rescued through a window and transported in serious condition to Emanuel Hospital's Burn Center, suffering from smoke inhalation and burns.
Due to the urgency, fire crews transported the patient in their truck as the ambulance was still 10 minutes away.
During the rescue, a firefighter sustained a back injury and was taken to the hospital for evaluation.

The fire spread to a nearby apartment, leading to the hospitalization of another resident with minor injuries and smoke inhalation concerns.
Tragically, one dog and one cat died in the fire, though it remains unclear which apartment they belonged to.
The Red Cross and Animal Control were dispatched to assist three displaced residents and manage the removal of the deceased pets.
The fire was contained before reaching the attic or other apartments. The cause of the fire is under investigation, and authorities urge anyone with information to contact them.
Shortly after, a second incident was reported at a high-rise at 655 NW Hoyt St. Engine 4 arrived to find no visible fire, but audible alarms were sounding.
Crews discovered an unattended incense had ignited nearby paper items on the fifth floor. The small fire was quickly extinguished without activating the sprinkler system, and the incident was resolved.
Portland Fire & Rescue reminds residents of the dangers of unattended candles and incense, urging responsible use to prevent potential disasters. They also expressed gratitude to their partners, including BOEC, PPD, PGE, Red Cross, and Animal Control, for their assistance.

content:
Residents fear deadly blaze in tower block with 'fire doors so bad a postman got trapped'
People living in a Brierley Hill tower say Dudley Council is fixing the wrong thing to stop fire doors staying open causing safety concerns
Residents of a Brierley Hill block of flats have spoken out about 'botched repairs' and perceived fire risks in their high rise block.
Diane Hobley said she had been raising concerns about the Dudley Council-owned Dean Court for 16 years but claimed she had not been taken seriously.
Mrs Hobley, aged 73, said fire doors on landings are blown open by wind coming through ventilation slats on the opposite wall and then do not close properly, creating a risk that fire could spread through the building.

Read more: Send parents demand action on special needs during poignant protest
Mrs Hobley said: "Gradually it got worse, the doors just wouldn't close. The council has tinkered with the doors, at one time they sent someone out every day to adjust the closer.
"They adjusted it and we couldn't open the door, the postman got stuck.
"We had to push the door open for him to get out and then the opposite happened where it was permanently open."
Gaynor English, aged 45, added: "They are trying to do things but they are not doing the right things, if we do it ourselves they will take it down.
"Even our front doors are no good, I can see daylight through mine."
Mrs Hobley said: "It's the slats, it's nothing to do with the doors, you could go to B&Q, get a block of wood and nail it to the thing, it would only cost £10."
With disasters like the Grenfell Tower fire of 2017 in their thoughts, residents said they would not be willing to wait in their homes during an emergency and trust the doors to keep flames at bay.
Mrs Hobley said: "It is in the back of your mind, especially if you smell an odd smell. I wouldn't wait an hour for a fire to be put out."
"It nearly did, nine years ago there was an old dear living opposite me – in the middle of the night I heard banging.
"It was the fire brigade, they were trying to break the door down.
"Smoke was coming out and one of the firemen came out with a pillow – she was smoking in bed so there was what could have been a fire."
A Dudley Council spokesperson told the Local Democracy Reporting Service the authority has emergency procedures to evacuate flats in the event of a fire.
The spokesperson added: "DMBC has a robust Fire Safety Management Plan aligned with the requirements of the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005 this ensures DMBC's residential communal living sites are managed and maintained in such a way as to reduce the risks associated with fire and building safety.
"The council responds to all concerns raised in relation to building safety and compliance.

title: Fort Kent woman , 56 , dies in apartment fire
content:
Fort Kent woman, 56, dies in apartment fire
FORT KENT, Maine (WGME) -- The Fire Marshal's Office is identifying the victim of a fatal fire in Fort Kent on Monday.
Fort Kent Fire and Rescue says crews responded to a fire at an apartment building on East Main Street around noon.
Officials say crews extinguished the fire on the first floor and found Ruth Charles of Fort Kent, 56. Crews tried to revive Charles, but she died.
Charles was reportedly taken to the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner for an autopsy.
Investigators say the fire was accidental and started in the bedroom of her apartment, where she lived alone.
Authorities attribute the cause to either an electrical fire or a candle.
Two other tenants were displaced temporarily, according to the Fire Marshal's Office.

content:
WARREN — No one was injured during an apartment fire Dec. 22 in Warren.
At 11:53 a.m. Dec. 22, Warren firefighters responded to a report of a fire in a building in the City Center Square apartments, on the corner of Karam and Washington Court boulevards, near 13 Mile Road and Van Dyke Avenue.
When firefighters arrived, they found smoke and fire in the attic of the apartment building, Warren Fire Commissioner Skip McAdams said. Firefighters were able to stop it from spreading further by making a trench cut in the roof of the building, he said.
McAdams said the fire was started by plumbers who were making repairs to a copper water line in the space behind a washing machine. The fire then spread to the second floor of the building, which has eight total apartments, and into the attic, he said.
While there were no injuries, at least two units were reportedly damaged. McAdams said firefighters had the fire under control at around 1 p.m. Firefighters were still on the scene at 1:45 p.m.
The Warren Fire Department was assisted by the Center Line and Detroit fire departments, as well as Warren police.

title: Man killed in Drexel Hill , Pennsylvania apartment blaze identified as longtime firefighter
content:
DREXEL HILL, Pa. (WPVI) -- The man who died in a Drexel Hill, Pa., apartment building blaze has been identified as a longtime firefighter.
The Lansdowne Fire Company identified the victim as Tony Rowley, who had also served as the department's vice president and ambulance lieutenant.
Rowley had been recently dealing with medical issues, the fire company said, and was at his home when the fire erupted in his apartment.
The fire erupted Saturday morning at the Llanerch Place Apartments on Township Line Road.
Viewer video shows Upper Darby Township firefighters making dramatic rescues as they tried to reach Rowley and his wife, who lived in the building.
Crews managed to reach them, but didn't realize the man they were carrying down the stairs was one of their own.
"To know that he gave 30 years of his life here in the community, have a little downfall, and get trapped by the very thing you've been protecting for so many years is a hard pill to swallow," said Michael Boyce, president of the Lansdowne Fire Company.
Rowley's wife, Anne, and seven other people were injured, including an Upper Darby firefighter who suffered burns but has been released from the hospital.
"Lansdowne firefighters would like to express our deepest gratitude to the UDFD for their valiant efforts attempting to save Tony and his family," the department said in a statement posted to social media. "Truly heroic."
About 75 people are displaced due to the blaze.
The cause of the fire remains under investigation.
Funeral arrangements for Rowley have not been released.

title: Fire at Ann Arbor Township apartment complex displaces residents before holidays
content:
ANN ARBOR TWP., MI – A fire that broke out in an Ann Arbor Township apartment building Sunday damaged several units and made the building temporarily uninhabitable.
Multiple fire crews responded Sunday, Dec. 21, to the apartment community Haven of Ann Arbor, 459 Village Green Blvd., for a reported fire in one of the buildings, Ann Arbor Township Fire Chief Mark Nicholai said.
Crews arrived to find a fire in the attic of one apartment building housing 24 individual apartments. The fire was brought under control, Nicholai said.
Of the 24 apartment units in the building, six sustained fire damage while the rest only sustained smoke and water damage, Nicholai said.
Six residents were displaced at the time of the fire and are being assisted by the American Red Cross, Nicholai said.
Due to the damage caused by the fire and the building’s utilities being shut off, the apartment building is uninhabitable at this time, Nicholai said.
There were many units affected by the fire belonging to tenants who are out of town for the holidays, Nicholai said.
One firefighter suffered minor injuries combating the blaze. He was treated at the scene and released, Nicholai said.
The cause of the fire remains under investigation.
The Ann Arbor Fire Department, Superior Township Fire Department, Ypsilanti Fire Department, Ypsilanti Township Fire Department, Pittsfield Township Fire Department, Scio Township Fire Department and the Northfield Township Fire Department assisted at the scene.

content:
A fire has destroyed two rooms in an eight-room residential building at Agboola Compound, Ita-Kure, in the Ilorin West Local Government Area of Kwara State, on Saturday.
According to Punch, the incident, which occurred at about 10:33 a.m., was contained by operatives of the Kwara State Fire Service, who prevented the fire from spreading to the remaining sections of the building.
Confirming the development in a statement on Saturday, the Head of Media and Publicity for the Kwara State Fire Service, Hassan Hakeem Adekunle, said preliminary findings showed that the inferno was triggered by a power surge.
Firefighters acted swiftly after receiving the distress call, adding that their intervention saved the compound from a more devastating loss.
“The coordinated and gallant efforts of our firefighters ensured that only two rooms were affected, while the remaining rooms were fully protected,” he said.
The Director of the Kwara State Fire Service, Falade Olumuyiwa, urged residents to prioritise electrical safety to prevent similar incidents, warning that many household fires are linked to poor wiring and substandard electrical materials.
He advised homeowners to install surge protectors and patronise certified professionals for routine checks on electrical systems.
The Director added, “Taking preventive steps significantly reduces the risk of electrical fires in residential areas. We urge residents to be vigilant and proactive.”
The service reaffirmed its commitment to safeguarding lives and property across Kwara State.
Kwara has recorded several fire outbreaks in recent weeks, many of which have been linked to electrical faults and careless handling of power appliances.
The state fire service has repeatedly appealed to residents to maintain safety standards, especially during the dry season, when fire incidents tend to increase.

content:
At 10:03 a.m. Thursday, May 21, the New York Fire Department received a report of a fire at the Skyview apartment complex at 5900 Arlington Ave. in Riverdale.
Dozens of people, along with their pets and children, stood outside the building as fire personnel rushed inside.
The fire was reported on the eighth floor of the 23-story high rise residential building. The fire department said 21 units with 79 fire and EMS personnel were dispatched to fight the wind-driven blaze, which was brought under control at 11:19 a.m. Two civilians were injured, and one was taken to the hospital, according to the fire department.
Four firefighters suffered non-critical injuries, and three of them were transported to hospitals, the department said.
Brennah Cody, whose mother Dawn lives on the 20th floor, was among those first to witness the chaos that morning. The two had left the apartment for a doctor’s appointment when, on the way downstairs, they encountered smoke beginning to build in hallways and stairwells.
Cody recalled coming outside to hear screaming coming from an eight-floor window, where she saw residents “trapped and screaming for help.”
“Some people that were living in the apartment were like on their balconies, and were crouching down, trying to cover themselves” while firefighters broke the windows, said Cody. She said she immediately called 911.
Stu and Lori Kolinsky, who live on the 12th floor, said they saw the fire trucks arriving from their window, and received a message from building management instructing everyone above the seventh floor to evacuate. As they moved through the building, they encountered thick, black smoke they said they couldn’t see through.
“We had to get through the black, not knowing what was facing us when we opened the door,” Stu Kolinsky said.
Residents Betty and Jose Figueroa live on the building’s 17th floor. Betty Figueroa said she was on Zoom when she received the message from building management, which also urged residents to close doors behind them to prevent the spread of the fire.
When the Figueroas exited their apartment, the thick smoke raised concerns about Jose Figueroa’s preexisting respiratory condition. As a precautionary measure, Betty Figueroa rushed back into the apartment to retrieve two surgical masks.
“There was a lot of commotion, people were nervous — practically everyone on the phone,” Jose Figueroa said, describing the scene that greeted them once they reached the lobby.
Bennett Pologe, a resident of the building for 20 years, said he first noticed the smoke by its smell.
“It smelled sort of oddly sweet, I thought someone was cooking something a little disgusting.” He said. “And then suddenly, there’s a banging on my door.”
That banging was building staff, telling Pologe he had to leave the building immediately. He had time to grab his backpack with his laptop inside, but said his elderly neighbor left with “just the shirt on her back.”
Cody said the apartment where the fire sparked had been under renovation for some time. Several residents noted work was ongoing most weekdays and told The Press they witnessed construction workers on site the morning of the blaze.
Skyview management did not respond for comment by press time.

title: Apartment fire in DeKalb County displaces residents , damages multiple units
content:
Apartment fire in DeKalb County displaces residents, damages multiple units
ATLANTA, Ga. (Atlanta News First) — An apartment fire in DeKalb County has displaced several residents.
“Hurtful. I hope I didn’t lose all of my stuff, but it probably got wet and smoke-damaged,” said Sylvia Williams, who lives in the apartment where the fire occurred.
The fire at 5959 Fairington Road in Stonecrest/Lithonia left residents temporarily homeless, with heavy damage visible to the upstairs units of the two-story building.
Residents said they first noticed something was wrong when they smelled smoke.
“My daughter started smelling the smoke, and she was like hearing stuff bumping, telling us to get out. So we ran downstairs, me and my youngest daughter, to come out,” Williams said. “And once the lady stopped banging, we opened the door so we could get out.”
“Before I even got to the front door, I heard this boom, boom, boom on the door, saying ‘come on out because my house is on fire,’” said another resident.
DeKalb County Fire Rescue said it is still unclear how the fire started, but confirmed there was fire damage to two units, along with smoke and water damage to others.
Officials said firefighters arrived to find flames blowing out the front door of the two-story, flat-roof apartment building. Crews performed top-side ventilation and used multiple saws and axes during the response.
“The folks were home when this fire started. They were able to get themselves out first, and then alert neighbors by knocking on doors to ensure everyone made it out safely,” said Capt. Jaeson Daniels, public information officer for DeKalb County Fire Rescue.
No injuries were reported, though residents are now trying to figure out their next steps. Some say they will temporarily stay with family.
“Basically, I don’t know. Money hasn’t come in, we only get paid every first of the month, so that’s pretty much it for now,” Williams said. “Me and my baby girl are going to be staying with my oldest daughter in Atlanta. We can make it through— with God, it’s going to be alright.”
The cause of the fire remains under investigation, according to DeKalb County Fire Rescue.

US News
2 killed, 11 injured in Bronx apartment building fire
Two people were killed and 11 others, including five firefighters, were injured when a fire tore through a five-story apartment building in the Bronx, according to FDNY officials. Firefighters rescued residents from windows and fire escapes.
The fire was reported at 1:32 p.m. on Tuesday at 660 East 187th Street, where officials said the building had stores on the first floor, two apartments behind the commercial space and six apartments on each floor above.
Deputy Assistant Chief Stacy Scanlon said two people were killed, two others were seriously injured, and nine more suffered minor injuries, including five firefighters and four civilians.
FDNY Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore said the response brought more than 84 fire and EMS units, with over 270 fire and EMS personnel sent to the scene.
Chief of fire operations Kevin Woods said firefighters arrived to find heavy fire on the first floor of the non-fireproof building, which had commercial space on the ground level, two apartments behind the stores and six apartments on each of the upper floors.
Woods said engine companies pushed inside with multiple handlines and knocked down fire on the lower floors, but crews had to switch to exterior operations when they reached the top floor because of the amount of fire and the condition of the building.
Ladder companies carried out rescues from both the front and rear of the building, Woods said. He said one person trapped at a window without access to a fire escape was rescued by portable ladder.
Woods said the building is more than 100 years old, mostly made of wood and heavily damaged. He said there is a risk of further collapse.
The cause of the fire is unknown. FDNY fire marshals are investigating.

Residents who were displaced by the fire are being helped by the American Red Cross.

Crews arrived to find a fire on a balcony extending into the roofline and an adjacent apartment at the complex on Madison Square Boulevard.
“The fire had moved into the attic, creating rapidly changing conditions that prompted a temporary evacuation of firefighters for safety,” LVFD said.

title: Firefighters contain West Jody Road brush fire before it reached apartments
content:
Firefighters contain West Jody Road brush fire before it reached apartments
FLORENCE COUNTY, S.C. (WPDE) — Florence County Fire Rescue crews contained a brush fire Sunday morning that threatened an apartment complex on West Jody Road.
Around 11:25 a.m., Engine 221 and Brush 225 responded to the 2200 block after reports of an outside fire. When crews arrived, they found a small but fast-spreading fire moving toward a nearby apartment building.
Firefighters were able to stop the fire before it reached the structure. However, a fence between the apartment complex and a construction site was damaged, and one building had minor heat damage.

No injuries were reported, and no residents were displaced. The cause of the fire is still under investigation.
This comes as a statewide burn ban is in place. Officials are continuing to remind residents that the dry weather and windy conditions can cause fires to spread quickly, so outdoor burning should be avoided.

content:
Local News
Fire displaces family out of Fond du Lac apartment complex
The Fond du Lac Fire and Rescue department responded to a fire yesterday in an apartment building in the city.
at around 5:40 p.m., a fire was reported at the Brooke Street Loft Apartments at 16 N. Brooke Street. While en route, Fond du Lac County Communications advised responding units that a child might still be inside the affected apartment.
Upon arrival, firefighters initiated an immediate rescue operation and entered the building to search for the child. Despite heavy smoke conditions, crews were able to conduct a rapid and thorough search of the apartment, ultimately confirming it was unoccupied. The child was later located safe elsewhere within the building.
Investigation showed the fire originated in the kitchen area of the apartment and was quickly brought under control. The affected apartment sustained fire damage to the kitchen and smoke damage throughout, and is currently uninhabitable. Residents of the building evacuated during the incident, and a significant portion of the structure required ventilation due to smoke.
The cause and origin of the fire remain under investigation by Fond du Lac Fire Rescue Fire Investigators.

content:
New team to check cladding is safe across Nottingham after Grenfell Tower fire
After the Grenfell Tower fire in London, which killed 72 people, the Government introduced new fire safety rules
A new team of inspectors will check tall buildings across Nottingham are safe following the Grenfell Tower fire in 2017.
A number of buildings across the city are covered in combustible cladding, including Marco Island, a 13-storey residential block on Huntingdon Street, as well as the Litmus Building in the same area.
The cladding on these buildings is being rectified.
Nottingham City Council now says six temporary staff members are being employed for 23 months to assist with inspection work and enforcement in private rented properties and tall buildings.
They will work alongside Nottinghamshire Fire and Rescue Service to help address any problematic external cladding and any work that may be required as a result.
“The Government have provided funding to support the delivery of the Local Remediation Action Plan (LRAP), which, working with East Midlands Combined County Authority (EMCCA), Nottingham City Council will work to continue inspecting and enforcing standards in tall buildings to ensure they meet certain standards,” council documents say.
After the Grenfell Tower fire in London, which killed 72 people, the Government introduced new fire safety rules, including new measures for high-rise blocks of flats that are at least 18 metres or seven storeys high.
The Government last year further announced a new Remediation Bill, which will require landlords of buildings 18 metres or more in height to remove unsafe cladding by the end of 2029, or by the end of 2031 if the structure is between 11 to 18 metres.
The six new staff members will also help to enforce the council’s selective licensing scheme.
The Labour-led council has been running the scheme since August 2018, aiming to make rented properties safer for tenants by requiring landlords to meet certain standards.
The licence requires landlords to pay a fee and covers around 30,000 homes in the city.
Documents say there has been an “above expected level of selective licence applications that need inspections undertaken”.
The first scheme legally expired in 2023, and a new one is now in place.
Under the first scheme, a total of 666 improvements were made to 446 properties, which the council described as a success.
However some landlords said the fees meant they had no choice but to pass the costs on to tenants in the form of rent increases, and an audit report found this to be correct in some cases.
In total £640,973 will be spent on the new staff members, funded from the council’s own selective licensing income and Government grants.

Fire leaves seniors stuck in Paris apartments
Article content
A small kitchen fire in the tower of independent apartments at Telfer Place in Paris has created a big problem for tenants, trapping some in their apartments with no way to leave.
Since the March 11 fire, many of those on the highest floors of the 10-storey building, are stuck, due to the two elevators being incapacitated and an inability for some to get down the multiple flights of stairs.
Recommended Videos
A spokesperson for Extendicare — which only recently purchased the complex, which includes a long-term care facility and assisted living space — said water from the sprinklers took the elevators out of service and, for safety reasons, each must be fixed and inspected in accordance with TSSA requirements before they can be used again.
“They told me repairs could take a month or they might even have to replace the elevator,” said one person who hasn’t been able to leave.
Extendicare is working to temporarily relocate people to other spots on the property while others have chosen to go home with family members or made alternative arrangements for accommodations while repairs are done.
But a small number of people are still stuck.
“They’ve been held hostage, trapped,” said a family member worried about a relative.
“It’s not a good take on why an elevator needs so much time to repair in such trying circumstances.”
Another family member said the situation seems to be no one’s fault.
“It’s just an unfortunate turn of events.”
An Extendicare spokesperson said additional staff are working to support the residents who remain in the building by knocking on doors to conduct regular wellness checks, delivering meals and groceries where needed, and making arrangements to relocate residents where possible.
“We recognize the disruption this has caused and our priority continues to be safety and well-being while repairs are being completed,” said an Extendicare spokesperson.
She noted an expedited repair plan is in place, however, the work will likely take weeks to complete because at least one elevator part has to be manufactured before being installed.
The fire, started in a tenant’s kitchen, was extinguished by the building’s sprinkler system said Fire Chief Darren Watson.
Normally, the elevators can be reset when the alarms go off but, in this case, the water caused an additional problem, he said.
While many tenants on floors six, seven and eight were evacuated, some simply couldn’t leave due to limited mobility.
“It was very frightening and the alarms were so loud you had to hold your head,” said one person about the incident.
Since some couldn’t negotiate the stairs, tenants, including some with their walkers, were directed to huddle in a stairwell for about half an hour.
Meanwhile, Extendicare said team members are providing individualized support to those affected through frequent communication and will continue to keep residents informed and supported.

title: Person dies in Jane and Finch apartment fire
North York highrise fire : 1 dead
content:
One person pulled from an apartment building unit that caught fire in North York has died, say officials.
Speaking with the media at the scene on Tuesday afternoon, Toronto Fire Services Cmdr. Robert Hewson said crews were called to a highrise at 5 Needle Firway, near Finch Avenue West and Jane Street, just before 12:15 p.m. after receiving 911 calls about a fire near the top floor of the building.
Upon arrival, firefighters encountered flames and saw black smoke coming from the penthouse level of the building, Hewson said.
They then made entry and rescued a person from a unit on the 12th floor.
“Crews made an aggressive attack on the fire and a very quick subsequent rescue. Unfortunately, the occupant of the building succumbed to their injuries,” he said, adding that investigators are on the scene waiting until the overhaul is completed before commencing their investigation.
“Condolences from Toronto Fire Services to friends and family.”
The commander said it appears that the fire was contained to the apartment of origin.
The cause and circumstances of the fire are unknown.
Toronto fire said primary and secondary searches are complete and the fire is now out.
‘Systems in place for calls like this’
Hewson went on to say that battling fires in highrises presents some unique challenges as they take about twice as many staff.
“You’re dealing with elevators and we only put a certain amount of firefighters in the elevator to start, and we start to utilize stairwell, and it’s a coordinated effort. It does take more time, but we also send a lot more crews, staff, firefighters to the scene,” he said.
“We have systems in place for calls like this.”
The investigation into the cause, origin, and circumstances of this fire, which is a joint effort between Toronto police, the Ontario Fire Marshal’s office and our own TFS investigators, is in the early stages, Hewson said.

Federal Fire Service Launches Nationwide Audit Of Buildings After Afriland Tower Blaze
content:
The Federal Fire Service (FFS) has begun a nationwide audit of public and private buildings across Nigeria to ensure compliance with fire safety regulations and improve national preparedness against emergencies.
The exercise, which commenced on Wednesday in Abuja, is being coordinated by the Task Force on Public and Private Building Audit, inaugurated by the Controller General of the FFS, Olumode Samuel Adeyemi (FCNA, ACTI), on October 14, 2025.
According to the Service, the initiative was prompted by the recent Afriland Tower fire incident in Lagos, which underscored the urgent need for stricter enforcement of fire safety standards nationwide.
A Shift Toward Prevention and Preparedness
Speaking at the launch, Controller General Adeyemi emphasized that the audit represents a major step in the Service’s strategy to prioritize fire prevention, preparedness, and compliance enforcement under the National Fire Safety Code.
“Safety consciousness and adherence to regulations remain the most effective ways to protect lives and property across the country,” Adeyemi said.
He explained that the audit will be extended to all State Fire Commands to ensure that both public and private structures comply with established fire safety requirements, including the installation of extinguishers, smoke detectors, emergency exits, and fire alarms.
Nationwide Implementation
The FFS announced that the exercise will cover offices, schools, hospitals, hotels, markets, high-rise buildings, and residential complexes, adding that the inspection teams will also evaluate risk assessment documentation, evacuation procedures, and safety training compliance.
The Service appealed to property owners, managers, and occupants to cooperate with officials for a transparent and effective inspection process.
“Fire safety is a shared duty,” Adeyemi stated, clarifying that the assessment was not designed to penalize but to foster a culture of prevention and accountability in building management.
Post-Afriland Tower Response
The Afriland Tower fire, which occurred in September 2025 in Lagos, had raised fresh concerns about building safety standards in Nigeria’s commercial hubs. The incident caused widespread panic and prompted renewed scrutiny of fire risk management in both private and government-owned properties.
Officials say lessons learned from the incident are guiding the current nationwide safety review to ensure that similar disasters are prevented through proactive enforcement.
Adeyemi added that the audit would be followed by public sensitization campaigns and capacity building for safety officers across states to sustain the culture of prevention.
A Call for Collective Responsibility
The FFS reiterated that while it is responsible for enforcement, citizen participation remains vital in achieving fire-safe communities.
“Every building inspected is a life potentially saved,” Adeyemi said. “Together, we can build a culture where fire safety becomes a daily responsibility, not an afterthought.”

content:
South Korean police said they would seek an arrest warrant for a woman who set fire to her apartment building while trying to kill a cockroach with an improvised flamethrower, local media report.
One of the woman's neighbours died after falling to the ground in a failed attempt to escape through a window.
The woman, who is in her 20s, told police that she tried to torch a cockroach with a lighter and a flammable spray, adding she had used the method before. But on Monday, items in her home caught fire.
Police in the northern city of Osan said the woman could be charged with accidentally starting a fire and causing death by negligence.
Blasting cockroaches - with blowtorches or homemade flamethrowers - have emerged as a novel way of getting rid of house pests, made popular by videos on social media.
In 2018, an Australian man set fire to his kitchen while trying to kill cockroaches with a homemade flamethrower made from insect spray.
The woman who died in the Osan city fire, a Chinese national in her 30s, lived on the fifth floor of the building with her husband and two-month-old baby.
When they realised that a fire had broken out, the couple opened their home window and called for help.
They handed their baby through the window to a neighbour in the adjacent block, before trying to evacuate themselves.
The woman's husband managed to climb over to the next block. She tried to do the same, but fell from the window. She was taken to the hospital and pronounced dead hours later.
Police said they believed the couple had tried escaping through the window because thick smoke from the fire had blocked the stairway, local media report.
The building houses commercial shops on its first floor and 32 residential units from its second to fifth floor.
Eight other residents suffered from smoke inhalation because of the fire.

Two Head to Hospital After Apartment Fire in Sherman Oaks
content:
Two people were injured as flames roared through the upper floor of a two-story apartment building in Sherman Oaks Thursday, leading to a protracted battle by firefighters.
The fire was reported at 8:54 a.m. Thursday in a garden-style apartment building at 14248 W. Dickens St., near the intersection of Ventura and Beverly Glen boulevards, according to the Los Angeles Fire Department.
Crews evacuated residents and cut holes in the roof to ventilate the structure as flames shot through the openings.
About 80 firefighters joined the battle and put the stubborn blaze out in two hours and 34 minutes, according to the LAFD.
Two patients were taken to hospitals. One was a 69-year-old woman who had shortness of breath, possibly after sustaining smoke inhalation. The other was a man of undisclosed age whose condition was not immediately known, said the LAFD’s Jennifer Middleton.
“Seven units/apartments were impacted by the fire,” she said, adding that three were deemed uninhabitable.
Eight adults were displaced and the Red Cross was providing support for the victims. Crews saved two dogs from the affected second-floor apartment, where they contained the fire.
The canines’ owner took possession of the dogs to take them to a veterinarian, Middleton said.
The LAFD’s Arson unit was investigating the cause of the fire, she said.
“LAFD companies will remain on scene for an extended period of time completing thorough overhaul procedures,” Middleton said.

Rockford Fire: Apartment kitchen goes up in flames while man takes his dog for a walk
ROCKFORD, Ill. (WIFR) - One man is displaced after a fire at his Rockford apartment.
Around 3 p.m. Monday, firefighters were called to a two-story apartment building in the 100 block of N. Rockton Ave. for a fire.
First responders report seeing heavy smoke and flames with zero visibility.
Firefighters attacked the source of the fire, but they learned that it extended from the first floor walls and up to the second story, which was vacant.
A second hose was used to extinguish the hidden fire in the walls.
The Rockford Fire Department says a man was heating up oil in preparation to cook food, took his dog for a walk and forgot his stove was on. When he got back home, he says the kitchen of his first-floor apartment was engulfed in flames. He got out of the house and the neighbors called for help. A report from the fire department also notes smoke detectors were present and working in the building.

title: Kolonos Apartment Fire : Woman Final Cry for Help
content:
‘Help, help, I’m drowning!’ — those were the desperate cries heard from a woman found dead alongside a man in an apartment fire in Kolonos, Athens, early Saturday morning (18.04.2026). The blaze broke out under unclear circumstances around 4:30 a.m. on the third floor of a residential building on Argous and Platonos Streets.
Panic, Screams, and Rapid Spread
According to eyewitnesses, loud voices and a violent argument were heard coming from the apartment shortly before the fire erupted — some even reported sounds of furniture being thrown. Residents described scenes of panic: the woman was seen pounding on the door and shouting for help. Minutes later, flames became visible from neighboring apartments.
Emergency Response and Tragic Outcome
Firefighters responded immediately with four vehicles and a specialized aerial ladder platform. They managed to extract both individuals unconscious from the smoke-filled unit. Shortly thereafter, their deaths were confirmed.
Victims and Background
The apartment belongs to an elderly woman who has lived in a nursing home for several years; her son had been residing there. Authorities are currently identifying the male victim — believed to be around 50 years old — with assistance from his aunt, who is present at the police station. Neighbors say both victims were substance users.
A neighbor recounted: ‘We heard voices around 5 a.m., then a fierce argument between the man and woman — things crashing, like furniture breaking. Then I heard a woman banging on the door, screaming “Help, I’m drowning!” I went out onto my balcony to see what was happening and heard people in the hallway talking to her, so I went back inside. But the banging and screams continued — then I smelled smoke. I got up and left. I live in the adjacent building, on the first floor. By about 5:20 a.m., we realized something serious was happening. By 5:30, flames were already visible. We saw it start in the right-side apartment on the third floor and quickly spread to the one on the left.’
Footage and Further Details
News site newsit.gr has published video footage showing the rapid escalation of the fire in the Kolonos apartment. Neighbors clarified that the woman found with the man was not his sister — but his partner, also approximately 50 years old.
For safety reasons, other residents of the building were evacuated. The fire caused extensive damage to the structure. The cause remains officially unknown. Investigators are exploring all possibilities — including a potential gas leak — while the reported altercation prior to the blaze adds further complexity to the case.

title: Siblings , ages 1 and 3 , killed in apartment fire
content:
Siblings, ages 1 and 3, killed in apartment fire
BOWLING GREEN, Ky. (WBKO/Gray News) - Two young children died after a fire tore through a unit at a Kentucky apartment building.
The fire started in the early morning on March 12 at a Bowling Green apartment, the fire department said.
The two children who died were identified by family members as 3-year-old Dominic and his 1-year-old sister, Aura.
The victims’ aunt, Destaney Handy, said the children’s mother woke to the smell of smoke and discovered the apartment was on fire.
“My sister, when I was talking to her yesterday, she just said she woke up from the smell of smoke and realized that her apartment was on fire. She just kept saying to me, ‘Destaney, I tried to get to them. I tried to get to them,’” Handy said.
Handy, who lives in Iowa, said she had not yet met Dominic or Aura in person, but had plans to visit them this summer.
“Since I live so far away from them, I hadn’t had the opportunity yet to be able to go out there to meet them. I just don’t know how to fathom that the only time I’m going to be able to see them is in a casket. I never got to hold them. I never got to meet them, but from everything that I know and from everything that I’ve learned, they were amazing. They were amazing kids,” Handy said.
Handy described the family’s state as devastated.
“She’s just devastated. We’re all just devastated. This is like something that feels unreal, like it’s some kind of nightmare that we’re hoping that we can wake up from,” Handy added.
Handy created a GoFundMe to help cover funeral costs for Dominic and Aura.
The family said they appreciate the community’s continued support.

दिल्ली के पालम स्थित साध नगर में एक रिहायशी 4 मंजिला बिल्डिंग में बुधवार सुबह करीब 7 बजे भीषण आग लग गई। हादसे में 9 लोगों की मौत हो गई, जिनमें 3 नाबालिग लड़कियां शामिल हैं। 2 लोगों ने जान बचाने के लिए बिल्डिंग से छलांग लगा दी।
दोनों को गंभीर चोटें आई हैं। दिल्ली फायर सर्विस (DFS) के कर्मियों ने 10 लोगों का रेक्स्यू किया है। इनमें 3 लोग घायल हैं। करीब 30 फायर ब्रिगेड मौके पर मौजूद हैं। आग पर काबू पा लिया गया है। फिलहाल आग लगने के कारणों का पता नहीं चल पाया है।
स्थानीय लोगों के अनुसार, आग शॉर्ट सर्किट के कारण लगी और तेजी से फैल गई। इमारत में उस समय 10-15 लोग मौजूद थे। इनमें कुछ शव बरामद किए जा चुके हैं। मृतकों की संख्या बढ़ने की आशंका है।
हादसे से जुड़ी 5 तस्वीरें…
दो घायलों का इलाज IGI अस्पताल में चल रहा
न्यूज एजेंसी IANS के मुताबिक, बिल्डिंग के बेसमेंट, ग्राउंड और फर्स्ट फ्लोर पर कपड़े और कॉस्मेटिक सामान के स्टोरेज के लिए किया जा रहा था। सेकेंड और थर्ड फ्लोर पर लोग रहते थे। चौथे फ्लोर पर एक टिन शेड बना हुआ था। आग की लपटें वहां तक पहुंच गई थीं।
घटना में मारे गए 8 लोगों के शव मणिपाल अस्पताल और एक महिला का शव IGI अस्पताल लाया गया था। घायलों में दो का इलाज IGI अस्पताल में चल रहा है, जबकि एक व्यक्ति को सफदरजंग अस्पताल में भर्ती कराया गया है।
मृतकों में प्रवेश (33), कमल (39), आशु (35), लाडो (70), हिमांशी (22), दीपिका (28) और तीन नाबालिग लड़कियां (15, 6 और 3 साल) शामिल हैं। अनिल (32) और 2 साल की एक बच्ची IGI अस्पताल में भर्ती हैं। सफदरजंग अस्पताल में भर्ती सचिन (29) लगभग 25% झुलस चुके हैं।
अधिकारी बोले- नीचे लपटें और ऊपर घना धुआं था
दिल्ली फायर सर्विस के अधिकारी एस. के. दुआ ने बताया कि आग सुबह करीब 7 बजे लगी थी। जब हमारी पहली टीम मौके पर पहुंची, तो नीचे आग की लपटें और ऊपर घना धुआं था। हमारे पहुंचने से पहले दो लोग इमारत से कूद गए थे, जिन्हें लोगों ने अस्पताल पहुंचाया।
अधिकारी के मुताबिक, अभी यह स्पष्ट नहीं है कि कितने लोग घायल हैं। आग पर अब पूरी तरह काबू पा लिया गया है, हालांकि कूलिंग ऑपरेशन जारी है। इसके बाद बिल्डिंग में एक बार फिर सर्च और रेस्क्यू किया जाएगा।
वहीं, NDRF के डिप्टी इंस्पेक्टर विक्की रांगा ने कहा बताया कि वे 10 मिनट के भीतर मौके पर पहुंच गए थे। तब तक दिल्ली फायर सर्विस और अन्य एजेंसियां आग बुझाने में लगी थीं। बिल्डिंग अंदर से काफी क्षतिग्रस्त हो गई है, ऐसे में रेस्क्यू ऑपरेशन करना बड़ी चुनौती है। एहतियात के तौर पर आसपास की इमारतों को भी खाली करा लिया गया है।
PM ने मृतकों के परिजनों को ₹2 लाख मुआवजे का ऐलान किया
पालम आग हादसे पर प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी ने शोक जताते हुए मुआवजे का ऐलान किया है। प्रधानमंत्री ने कहा कि हादसे में जान गंवाने वालों के परिजनों को प्रधानमंत्री राष्ट्रीय राहत कोष (PMNRF) से ₹2 लाख की आर्थिक सहायता दी जाएगी, जबकि घायलों को ₹50 हजार दिए जाएंगे।
इस बीच कांग्रेस सांसद प्रियंका गांधी ने भी घटना पर दुख जताया और पार्टी कार्यकर्ताओं से पीड़ितों की मदद करने की अपील की।
इंदौर में EV चार्जिंग के दौरान घर जला, 8 लोगों की मौत

Possible Arson Under Investigation After Early Morning Fire at Portland Apartment Building – The Maine Wire
content:
PORTLAND, Maine — Police and fire investigators are examining a possible arson after an early morning fire Monday at an apartment building on Bishop Street.
According to authorities, the Portland Fire Department responded at approximately 2:43 a.m. on March 16, 2026, to a fire alarm at Huston Commons, located at 72 Bishop Street. When the first fire units arrived on scene, they observed smoke coming from a third-floor apartment unit inside the building.
Firefighters located a small fire within the unit and were able to extinguish it quickly.
Investigators from the Portland Fire Department responded to the scene and began working alongside the Portland Police Department to determine the cause of the fire.
During the course of the investigation, detectives with the Portland Police Department’s Criminal Investigations Division discovered suspicious materials inside the apartment. The discovery prompted a response from the department’s Hazardous Device Unit (HDU).
After examining the materials, the Hazardous Device Unit determined that there was no threat, allowing investigators to safely continue their work at the scene.
Authorities say it appears the occupant of the apartment attempted to escape the building by lowering himself from a third-floor window using sheets tied together. The man ultimately fell to the ground and was transported to Maine Medical Center with non-life-threatening injuries.
The investigation into the suspected arson remains ongoing, and officials say charges are pending.
Police are asking anyone with information that may assist investigators in this or any other case to contact the Portland Police Department at 207-874-8575. Individuals may also submit information anonymously by texting the keyword PPDME and their message to 847411.

1 pulled from North York apartment following fire
content:
One person pulled from an apartment building unit that caught fire in North York has died, say officials.
Speaking with the media at the scene on Tuesday afternoon, Toronto Fire Services Cmdr. Robert Hewson said crews were called to a highrise at 5 Needle Firway, near Finch Avenue West and Jane Street, just before 12:15 p.m. after receiving 911 calls about a fire near the top floor of the building.
Upon arrival, firefighters encountered flames and saw black smoke coming from the penthouse level of the building, Hewson said.
They then made entry and rescued a person from a unit on the 12th floor.
“Crews made an aggressive attack on the fire and a very quick subsequent rescue. Unfortunately, the occupant of the building succumbed to their injuries,” he said, adding that investigators are on the scene waiting until the overhaul is completed before commencing their investigation.
“Condolences from Toronto Fire Services to friends and family.”
The commander said it appears that the fire was contained to the apartment of origin.
The cause and circumstances of the fire are unknown.
Toronto fire said primary and secondary searches are complete and the fire is now out.
‘Systems in place for calls like this’
Hewson went on to say that battling fires in highrises presents some unique challenges as they take about twice as many staff.
“You’re dealing with elevators and we only put a certain amount of firefighters in the elevator to start, and we start to utilize stairwell, and it’s a coordinated effort. It does take more time, but we also send a lot more crews, staff, firefighters to the scene,” he said.
“We have systems in place for calls like this.”
The investigation into the cause, origin, and circumstances of this fire, which is a joint effort between Toronto police, the Ontario Fire Marshal’s office and our own TFS investigators, is in the early stages, Hewson said.

The blaze erupted around 4 p.m. in a 50-square-meter unit at a 26-story residential complex on To Hieu Street, located near the beach in Nam Nha Trang Ward of Khanh Hoa Province. Nguyen Thanh Ha, Vice Chairman of the Khanh Hoa People’s Committee, confirmed that a man and a woman were killed. Their bodies were discovered in the bedroom, where the fire had caused significant damage.

Police completed their examination of the scene by 8:30 p.m.

SYRACUSE, N.Y. — The Syracuse Fire Department responded to a kitchen fire in a multi-story senior living apartment building on Crouse Avenue on the evening of Jan. 15.

title: Birmingham tower block fire live - more than 50 firefighters tackling blaze in Grade II building
content:
Birmingham tower block fire live - road remains shut after Grade II-listed building blaze
A fire which broke out in a historic high-rise building in Constitution Hill has been brought under control - but the road remains shut
A fire which broke out in a high rise Grade-II listed building in the centre of Birmingham. is now under control. But the main road it sits on remains closed.
The fire took hold at a building in Constitution Hill, Hockley. shortly before 7.30am on Friday (January 16).
It is the Grade II listed former HB Sale factory and office and one of the city's 'terracota treasures'.
Read more: Twenty firefighters called to city tower block blaze as smoke filled flats
West Midlands Fire Service said has said it initially sent eight crews, with more than 30 firefighters to the scene.
That was upscaled to 10 and then 13 crews before later being reduced to three.
The fire was in the fourth floor of the five-storey building which dates to the 19th century.
An eyewitness has told BirminghamLive: “Massive fire on Constitution Hill, Hockley. Avoid the area 20 firefighters everywhere.”
West Midlands Fire Service posted on X and said: “We have 8 crews in attendance at Constitution Hill, Hockley, where they have responded to Tall Building Fire. Please avoid the area, where possible.”
One man was injured in the fire and had to be taken to hospital - but his injuries from smoke inhalation are said to be minor.
The fire service said damping down has taken place and crews will return periodically to check the building.
Constitution Hill though remains closed due to 'electrical works'
This is a live breaking story and updates will follow below.
Our reporter has been back out to Constitutuion Hill and confirmed the road remains closed with a police cordon in place.
This is due to ongoing 'electrical works'. So avoid the area on your way home tonight.
While the fire is under control at the Grade II-listed former HB Sale building in Constitution Hill, there are ongoing issues meaning the road cannot be reopened.
West Midlands Fire Service has said its crews have completed 'damping down', ensuring the fire is out. But they will be making revisits.
But the main issue now appears to be problems with the electrics, meaning Constitution Hill remains closed in the busy evening period.
A spokesperson for the brigade has said: "Damping down has been completed. We expect to carry out several revisits throughout the afternoon and overnight.
"Constitution Hill remains closed in both directions due to electrical work taking place at the scene. Police colleagues remain in attendance."
A pub in Birmingham has opened late today due to the fire in Constitution Hill.
The Wolf, which is in the same road as the fire hit buiilding, was forced to delay opening to 1pm with cordons in place.
It posted in its Instagram story that it had to open late due to 'some early morning drama over the road'.
The venue is now open but only acccessible from its Water Street entrance.
The venue features in BirminghamLive's 26 best restaurants in the city for 2026 with its 'unreal value.
And it is celebrating its ninth birthday this weekend with limited release beers - so sneak in via Water Street if you can.
West Midlands Fire Service has said investigators are now at the scene of the Grade II-listed building fire in Constitution Hill to try and find the cause of the 'severe fire'.
It took hold in the fourth floor of the five-storey building shortly before 7.30am on Friday (January 16).
Flames were seen leaping out of a window and there were plumes of smoke as firefighters from 13 crews tackled the fire at its peak.
They have now been scaled back with three crews remaining.
But three roads remain shut, as the incident moves to an investigation phase.
A fire service spokesperson said: "Fire Investigators are working at the scene.
"Current road closures are:
- The junction of Water Street to Henrietta Street
- Constitution Hill to Henrietta Street
- Hampton Street to Henrietta Street.
"A building surveyor is in attendance, and specialist technical rescue firefighters are supporting the three crews at the scene. "
West Midlands Fire Service has provided a fresh update to say the building has been searched and everyone has been accounted for.
A spokesperson said: "A full, thorough search of the building has been undertaken and it has been confirmed that everyone has been accounted for.
"National Grid colleagues have also been in attendance, working to isolate a nearby substation.
"Firefighting continues but ambulance colleagues have left the incident.
"Constitution Hill remains closed. This incident will be scaled down to three fire engines shortly."
An update from the Safer Travel Police team has indicated that Constitution Hill, the scene of a fire in a historic Birmingham building, will remain shut for hours.
The team has posted on X and said: "Constitution Hill will remain closed until late afternoon, meaning the 16 & 74 services remain on diversion.
But "Following the earlier fire, Summer Lane has now reopened and the National Express West Midlands number 7 bus service is now running as normal. "
Here is the latest from our reporter Harry Leach at the scene:
West Midlands Fire Service has issued an update on its firefighting efforts at the Grade II-listed building in Constitution Hill.
It says firefighters are continuing to tackle the fire and are using breathing apparatus to do so. But it is asking people to avoid the area.
A spokesperson for the brigade said: "A multi-agency briefing between WMFS, Police and Ambulance colleagues, Cadent and Severn Trent Water has taken place at the scene.
"Firefighters wearing breathing apparatus are continuing their work to extinguish this fire.
"Police colleagues are supporting with traffic management.
"Bus routes are being diverted around this area due to our attendance. Routes 7, 16, 52 and 74 are on diversion via St Chads Queensway, Lancaster Street, Newtown Row and New John Street West. For live travel updates from National Express West Midlands, click here.
"Continue to avoid the area."
With Summer Lane reopening National Express has confirmed its 7 service is back to its normal route in both directions.
The bus firm said: "Summer Lane has reopened
"Number 7 is following the normal route in both directions
"We apologise for any disruption to your journey."
And Google's traffic map shows some red lines of slow moving traffic but some easing to yellow.
Emergency services appear to have scaled back their response slightly.
There are noticeably less ambulances, police vehicles and fire engines lining Constitution Hill than two hours ago.
West Midlands Road has confirmed Summer Lane (towards Constitution Hill) is now open.
But it added: "However, Constitution Hill/Old Snow Hill remain closed.
"Traffic is now able to turn left from Summer Lane up Old Snow Hill."
While National Express West Midlands has said one of its services - the number 7 is on its usual route but only into the city.
It said: "7 into CITY ONLY is following the normal route We apologise for any disruption to your journey."
The fire at one of Birmingham's historic and protected buildings has caused upset and bewilderment for locals.
It was seeing Birmingham 'lose its heritage' in real time.
One man, who chose not to be named, said it was “devastating” to see the Grade ll-listed building go up in flames. The dad, standing at the edge of the cordon, said: “I really hate seeing this kind of thing. I feel like Birmingham loses heritage all the time. “That’s through our own fault, mainly, I think, but also when things like this happen. It’s just devastating, really.”

“One minute, everything was fine, then all of a sudden...”
“It was frightening when we looked outside and saw how big it was.”
West Midlands Ambulance Service has confirmed one man has been injured in the fire.
He suffered smoke inhalation and has been taken to hospital, but his injuries are not thought to be too serious.

The bus company said: "Due to an Emergency service lead incident at Constitution Hill #Birmingham
"Buses 7, 16, 52 and 74 are on diversion via:
St Chads Queensway, Lancaster Street, Newtown Row and New John Street West
"We apologise for any disruption to your journey."
Our reporter is a the incident and has sent the following update.
He said: "A fire has broken out at a historic building on the corner of Constitution Hill and Summer Lane in Hockley this morning, with smoke and flames visible from the top floor. "Fire crews are currently tackling the blaze using an aerial ladder platform, with jets of water being directed at the upper levels of the building. "All three emergency services - fire, police and ambulance - are at the scene and the road has been cordoned off in several directions. "Fire engines and a number of ambulances are lined along the long street as crews work to bring the incident under control. "The cause of the fire is not yet known."
West Midlands Fire Service has said it now has 10 crews at the scene of the blaze in Constutution Hill.
A spokesman at fire control said the fire service received the call at 7.29am.
He said their were now 10 applainces at the site. But he referred BirminghamLive to West Midlands Police for more details.
Orange flames and smoke could be seen earlier coming from a top floor window at the 'terracotta' building in Consitution Hill.

title: 3 die in Uttara apartment fire
content:
News Flash
DHAKA, Jan 16, 2026 (BSS)- At least six people were killed in a devastating fire that broke out in a residential building in the city's Uttara area on Friday morning, authorities confirmed.
The six dead included two women, one man and a child. The names and identities of the other deceased are not yet known.
The fire erupted around 7:50 am in a flat on the second floor of a six- to seven-storey residential building on Road 18, Sector 11 in Uttara.
Fire Service and Civil Defence (FSCD) received the alert at 7:54 am and immediately dispatched firefighting units to the scene.
According to FSCD media officer Talha Bin Jasim, two fire units from Uttara Fire Station reached the building by 7:58 am, with more units joining shortly afterward.
Firefighters brought the blaze under control around 8:25 am and fully extinguished it by around 10:00 am.
Initially, three people were found dead at the scene, while 13 injured residents were taken to Kuwait Bangladesh Friendship Government Hospital for treatment.
Later, three more victims died while undergoing treatment, raising the death toll to six, said Uttara Division Deputy Commissioner of Police Shahriar Ali.
Fire service officials said the fire spread rapidly due to a large amount of furniture inside the affected flat.
Md Abdul Mannan, deputy assistant director of Fire Service Dhaka Zone-3, said the fire may have originated from an electrical short circuit, although the exact cause will be confirmed following an investigation.
The flames spread from the second floor to the third floor, worsening the situation and filling the building with thick smoke.
Local residents described scenes of panic and chaos as occupants struggled to escape the smoke-filled stairwells.
Authorities have launched an investigation into the incident and urged residents to strictly adhere to fire safety measures to prevent similar tragedies in the future.

title: Cause of fire at Salina apartment complex determined
content:
SALINE COUNTy —Investigators determined the fire at a Salina apartment complex on Wednesday afternoon was accidental and caused by careless discarding of smoking materials, according to a statement from the Salina Fire Department.
Just after 3p.m. Wednesday, crews were dispatched to The Ridge Apartment complex, 2363 Chapel Ridge after receiving reports of fire and smoke coming from the front of the two-story apartment building at the complex.
Upon arrival, firefighters found heavy fire and smoke conditions extending from the front of the building into the soffit with fire already extending into the attic and through the roof.
Crews immediately began fire suppression operations while also conducting a search for occupants in the affected apartment units. Due to the amount of active fire and potential for life safety issues, a second alarm was struck upon the arrival of the on-duty Battalion Chief.
The fire was brought under control within approximately 30 minutes, with crews remaining on scene for an extended period to ensure the fire was fully extinguished and to check for any extension into neighboring units.
While several residents were displaced as a result of the fire, all occupants were able to safely exit the building and there were no injuries to report.
The cause of the fire has been ruled as accidental and likely due to the careless discarding of smoking materials near the front of the building.
